definitions.explanation: The time of day around noon when people typically eat lunch. Roughly 11:30 AM to 1:30 PM.

examples.japanese: {昼|ひる}どきのレストランは{満席|まんせき}だった。
examples.english: The restaurant was fully booked at lunchtime.

examples.japanese: {昼|ひる}どきを{避|さ}けて{行|い}けば、{並|なら}ばなくて{済|す}む。
examples.english: If you go outside of the lunch rush, you won't have to wait in line.

notes:
Refers specifically to the period around noon associated with the lunch meal. The suffix どき means "time for" and creates a natural, colloquial feel.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {昼|ひる}どきの{混雑|こんざつ}: lunchtime crowds
- {昼|ひる}どきを{避|さ}ける: to avoid the lunch rush
- {昼|ひる}どきに{行|い}く: to go at lunchtime

RELATED WORDS:
- {昼食|ちゅうしょく}: lunch (formal)
- お{昼|ひる}: lunch (casual)
- {夕|ゆう}どき: around evening/dusk — uses the same どき pattern
- {食|た}べどき: the right time to eat something

USAGE:
Most commonly used when talking about restaurant crowding, meal timing, or scheduling around the midday period.
